video.title: Make $20K/Month Selling to Clients Who Don’t Flinch at Price

summary: Chris Koerner and regular guest Sam discuss one-person businesses that can reach $20K/month profit without employees. Sam describes testing an AI-written divorce book ($29 ebook, $17 bump, $300 back-end) sold via Facebook ads at roughly break-even CAC, then printing 300 physical copies until Facebook restricted the ads as 'personal hardship' targeting. Chris adds the idea of monetising the book buyers by referring them to divorce lawyers for pay-per-lead or consulting/referral fees, and extends it to niche legal books (DUI, car accident, etc.). The key takeaway is to test quickly rather than over-research, start with the simple pay-per-lead model, and that $20K/month solo is far easier than scaling to a million-dollar team business.

speakers.name: Sam
speakers.description: Recurring guest, runs the Grow Faster community, ecommerce/ads operator; tested the divorce book funnel

ideas.name: Divorce self-help book funnel (ebook + bump + back-end)
ideas.one_liner: Sell an AI-assisted 'how to win your divorce' ebook/printed book via Facebook ads with a $17 bump and $300 back-end programme.
ideas.business_model: One-off product sales (ebook/print book) plus order bump and back-end programme; possible lead resale
ideas.customer: People going through or facing a divorce (US)
ideas.problem: Divorce is expensive, emotional and people dislike their divorce attorneys; little non-lawyer material targets them
ideas.offer: $29 ebook 'How to Win Your Divorce', $17 negotiation training toolkit bump, $300 Financial Protection Protocol back-end; later a 200-page printed copy

pricing.model: Low-ticket front end with bump and back-end upsell
pricing.notes: AOV around $42 with bump; about 70% of buyers took the bump per Sam

acquisition_channels.details: Facebook/Meta ads, broad targeting, automatic placements, optimised for purchases using a pixel on the thank-you page; about $100/day; first week $500-700 spend. Ads later blocked from purchase optimisation as 'personal hardship' targeting.

quote.text: I do automatic placements, broad targeting. Facebook is smarter than us and will dictate the spend based on what you're trying to optimize for.
quote.speaker: Sam

acquisition_channels.details: Idea of theme pages about divorce or crazy divorce stories to move inventory for free (not tested).

ideas.delivery: Ebook delivered digitally (zero COGS); physical books printed (300 copies at about $6 each, about $8.50 landed with shipping) and shipped to customers; book written with ChatGPT then about 5 hours of refinement.
unit_economics_claims: Ebook $29, CAC about $40 at first, then about $40-45 CAC at break-even with AOV about $42
300 printed books cost about $6 each, about $8.50 shipped
ideas.startup_cost: About $500-700 initial ads plus about $3,000 for printed books; ebook version near zero
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: First week of ads (sales within days)

acquisition.how: Paid Meta ads with creative refresh are largely automatable, but needs human creative and policy-compliance handling; ad category restrictions are a risk.

onboarding.how: Funnel checkout with bump and upsell is automated software.

delivery.how: Ebook is instant; print-on-demand fulfilment can be automated, though Sam printed stock himself.

support.how: Order and shipping queries can be handled by an agent with a human check; a VA suggested for email.

uk_applicability.notes: Funnel works in UK but divorce law, lawyer market, pricing and Meta ad restrictions on personal hardship differ; the 50% divorce stat is US-framed (UK roughly 40%+).

risks: Facebook classified ads as targeting personal hardship, blocking purchase optimisation
Break-even CAC leaves no margin without upsells or lead resale
Unsold physical inventory in the garage

ideas.name: Divorce lead generation sold to lawyers
ideas.one_liner: Use book buyers as leads and sell them or referrals to divorce attorneys on pay-per-lead, per-signed-client or revenue-share terms.
ideas.business_model: Pay per lead, per signed client, or percentage of legal fees (framed as consulting fee)
ideas.problem: Lawyers pay very high costs per lead on Google and are burned out on poor-quality leads
ideas.offer: Pre-qualified leads from people who bought a niche book, delivered to lawyers at a fixed price per lead or per signed contract

pricing.model: Pay per lead, per signed contract, or revenue share
pricing.notes: Chris suggests 30% of fees collected (fees between $7K and $23K, attorney about $270/hr); a quarter of invoices is an alternative; all hypothetical

acquisition_channels.details: Phone two or three lawyers beforehand to agree terms, then build relationships and share close data to set pricing for other lawyers.
Book funnel ads act as the lead source, aiming for break-even on the book so leads cost nearly nothing.

ideas.delivery: Refer or send buyer details to lawyers; track which leads close by staying close to 2-3 lawyers; or just sell leads upfront and not worry about closing.
unit_economics_claims: 3% take rate on 300 back-end puts you at $900/day profit (Sam's hypothetical)
Lead costs could drop to about $10 net if book revenue offsets CAC
Legal Google clicks can cost up to $5,000 per lead (trucking accident)

acquisition.how: Ad funnel automated; lawyer partnership sourcing via cold email to firms (limited companies, PECR-allowed) is possible but relationship building needs a human.

onboarding.how: Agreeing terms and getting lawyers to share data needs human negotiation.

delivery.how: Lead routing by software is straightforward once buyers are opted in.

billing.how: Invoicing per lead is automatable; revenue-share tracking is harder.

support.how: Lawyer relationship follow-up on closed deals is mostly human.

uk_applicability.notes: UK solicitors are regulated by the SRA, which restricts referral fees and requires disclosure; the 'consultant' workaround is US-state specific. Lead data needs UK GDPR consent to pass on. Possible with lead-gen compliant structure but heavily changed.

risks: US state rules on non-lawyers taking referral fees
Lawyers may run away without paying on revenue-share
Lawyers poor at closing leads will stop buying
Trade-off between hands-on trust and profitability

tactics.name: Fast test of a book funnel
steps: Spot a big painful market and check keywords briefly
Build a two-step funnel on Perspective
Run broad Meta ads, automatic placements, about $100/day, optimise for purchases with a pixel on the thank-you page
Read signal from CAC versus price
Move to ClickFunnels for bump and upsell offers

tactics.name: Raise AOV with bump and back-end
steps: Add a $17 bump at checkout before payment
Aim to bring AOV near CAC so ads break even

tactics.name: Improve conversion by upgrading to a physical book
steps: Rewrite the AI draft with about 5 hours of work
Market it as a real shipped book to lift conversion

tactics.name: Start lead gen with the simplest pay-per-lead deal
steps: Sell leads upfront at a low price (e.g. $100) to avoid babysitting lawyers
Build relationships with 2-3 lawyers who share close data
After about 3 months use data to price for lawyers you do not know
Raise prices or move to revenue share once close rates are proven

tactics.name: Benchmark against your own past performance
steps: Compare cost per click and conversion to your own history
Ask whether you can make your own math work

lessons.lesson: Running one funnel teaches copywriting, landing pages and ads, skills reusable across any market.
Break-even customer acquisition via a low-ticket product, with profit from a back-end or lead sale, is a strong model.
Choose the lower-touch, lower-profit version first so you do not burn out before learning.
Sell the same lead to the buyer, not the vulnerable consumer: monetising lawyers with money to spend.
Going from a $20K/month solo business to a million-dollar team business adds disproportionate work, stress and people for modest extra profit.

quote.text: It's four times more revenue for maybe two times more profit and like six times more work
quote.speaker: Sam

lessons.lesson: Pay-per-lead is an arbitrage between wholesale and retail lead cost, and a front-end product can subsidise lead cost.
Shrink goals to a quarter million a year solo rather than chasing yachts; doubling income and halving stress.
Execution matters more than ideas; people given a good idea often do nothing.

evidence_quality.rationale: Sam gives first-hand but partial numbers on a break-even test with no profit proven; the lead-resale economics and $20K/month path are hypothetical.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Sam runs the Grow Faster community; Chris sells TK Owners; Beehiiv sponsor read; both promote Perspective.
